title: Zenith Payments - POC Timeline & Milestones
summary: POC scoping focused on timeline and milestones for a 6-week pilot: kickoff, access setup, initial ingestion & baseline benchmarks, mid-point performance review, and executive readout. Discussed success criteria (latency targets, cost per request, accuracy thresholds), workload sizing (expected qps and token distribution), and benchmark plan including Redwood-hosted and dedicated runs. Agreed next steps: schedule kickoff, exchange security docs, provide sample dataset and API keys, draft SOW and pricing.
next_steps: Schedule POC kickoff for week of 2026-01-20 (Sam)
Zenith to provide 2 weeks of sample traffic + schema (Priya)
Sam to send draft SOW and pricing (Sam)
Set up initial Redwood test tenant and API keys (Jordan)
action_items: Sam Parker: Draft SOW and pricing sheet by 2026-01-13
Maya Lin: Share SOC2 report, encryption/KMS notes, and private deployment checklist by 2026-01-12
Priya Nair: Share sample dataset (anonymized) and traffic profile by 2026-01-14
Jordan Wu: Provision test tenant and create API keys; delivery by 2026-01-15
Daniel Cho: Arrange network contact for VPC peering discussion by 2026-01-16
transcript:
[00:00] Sam Parker: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sam, AE on the Redwood side, and with me is Maya Lin, our SE, and Jordan from solutions. Um, is that right?
[00:10] Alex Rivera: Yeah hi, Alex here, CTO at Zenith. Thanks, Sam. Priya and Daniel also on.
[00:16] Priya Nair: Hi all. Real quick, we want to make sure this POC maps to our billing flow and fraud detection endpoints.
[00:25] Maya Lin: Great, good to know. Today we'd like to align on success criteria, workload sizing, the benchmark plan, and a concrete timeline with milestones — kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout.
[00:38] Daniel Cho: Sounds good. We're mainly concerned about latency during peak auth flows and cost per thousand tokens since we do lots of short requests. Also compliance — we need to know how logs, encryption, and residency are handled.
[00:51] Sam Parker: Totally. I'll run through the proposed 6-week timeline, then Maya will walk through the benchmark plan and the metrics we'll measure, and then we can map responsibilities.
[01:00] Sam Parker: Week 0: Kickoff and access setup. Week 1-2: Ingest sample traffic and run baseline benchmarks on hosted Redwood instances. Week 3-4: Run dedicated capacity tests and KV cache enabled paths, measure throughput and tail latency. Week 5: Mid-point review and any tuning. Week 6: Exec readout and decision.
[01:24] Priya Nair: Is the expectation to test both hosted and dedicated? We might only need hosted for the pilot but would like to understand dedicated numbers for forecast.
[01:33] Maya Lin: We recommend both — hosted for fastest time-to-value and dedicated numbers to project unit economics. For the pilot we'll run initial workloads on hosted, then spin up a dedicated pool for comparative benchmarks.
[01:45] Alex Rivera: Success criteria — what do you need from us? Our internal bar is p95 auth latency <= 120ms and cost <= $0.10 per 1k tokens for our mid-term forecast. Accuracy is tricky; we want false positive rate not to exceed current rule-based baseline.
[02:05] Maya Lin: That's clear. For the POC let's define primary success metrics: p95 latency target (your 120ms), tail latency behavior, throughput sustaining 250 qps during peak windows, and inference cost delta compared to your current baseline. For accuracy we'll run a labeled eval set to compare false positive/negative rates.
[02:25] Daniel Cho: 250 qps is peak; average is around 40 qps. Typical requests are short — 30–50 tokens per request, but we also have longer reconciliation jobs that are ~800 tokens but low frequency.
[02:40] Jordan Wu: Good to know. We'll ask for a traffic histogram and token distribution so we can size batching and KV cache recommendations.
[02:50] Priya Nair: What about data residency? For some finance flows we need EU-only data handling.
[02:56] Maya Lin: We support region pinning — you can run the POC in our EU region or a private deployment. We'll include details in the security pack.
[03:06] Sam Parker: Benchmarks: we'll run synthetic replay of sample traffic plus a set of benchmark prompts. Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, throughput (sustained qps), and quality metrics from labeled eval.
[03:20] Alex Rivera: Can you run both quantized model variants? We want to see tradeoffs on CPU/GPU cost.
[03:26] Maya Lin: Yes — we'll run 16-bit and 8-bit quantized variants where supported, and a couple of model sizes to show the cost/perf curve. We'll log per-token timing and memory utilization.
[03:36] Priya Nair: Access setup — what do you need for us to get started?
[03:40] Jordan Wu: We'll need a sample dataset, schema, a histogram of qps and token distributions, a list of example endpoints, and an account admin to set up API keys. For dedicated tests we'll request VPC peering info or a staging cluster credential depending on the option you choose.
[03:56] Daniel Cho: On VPC peering, we have a network team — I'll get the contact, but we prefer using Redwood's private deployment for sensitive flows.
[04:05] Maya Lin: Noted. For the POC we'll provision a test tenant in the region you prefer and give scoped API keys with configurable retention.
[04:14] Sam Parker: Timeline check — if kickoff is week of 2026-01-20, access and sample data need to arrive by 2026-01-14 to keep the schedule.
[04:24] Priya Nair: We can aim for that.
[04:26] Alex Rivera: On stakeholders, the mid-point review should include our VP Eng and Head of Product; exec readout will include our COO.
[04:35] Maya Lin: We'll prepare a mid-point slide deck with perf graphs and tuning recommendations, and an exec-ready one pager summarizing outcomes and recommended next steps.
[04:45] Daniel Cho: For benchmarks, can Redwood provide a comparison to a baseline like our current rule engine?
[04:50] Maya Lin: Yes, please provide labeled outputs from your current system for a sample set; we'll run side-by-side evals.
[04:56] Sam Parker: Pricing — we'll send a pilot price for the 6-week POC and optional dedicated pricing estimates; the SOW will call out what counts as billable (e.g., dedicated run hours).
[05:07] Priya Nair: Any gotchas for onboarding? We have strict audit requirements and need to ensure log retention and redaction policies are honored.
[05:14] Maya Lin: We'll share our compliance pack. We support KMS-backed key management, field-level redaction patterns, and audit logs that can be shipped to your SIEM. We'll include those links in the docs.
[05:27] Alex Rivera: Who will own the day-to-day touchpoint from Redwood?
[05:31] Sam Parker: I'll be the AE owner and coordinate timeline; Maya and Jordan will be the technical leads.
[05:36] Daniel Cho: Ok. 
[05:38] Sam Parker: Quick recap of milestones: Kickoff (week of Jan 20) — access and API keys provisioned; Baseline hosted benchmarks (week 1-2) — ingest sample traffic and run synthetic replay; Dedicated comparative tests (week 3-4) — enable dedicated pool, KV cache experiments; Mid-point review (end of week 5) — present tuning, decide next steps; Exec readout (week 6) — summary and recommendation.
[06:05] Priya Nair: That looks good. Can you include a timeline slide with dates?
[06:09] Sam Parker: Yes — I'll include target dates in the SOW.
[06:13] Alex Rivera: For the mid-point, we'd like jitter and tail latency breakdowns per model variant.
[06:18] Maya Lin: We'll include p99 and per-model tail latency graphs plus token-level timing.
[06:24] Jordan Wu: On instrumentation we'll add trace hooks to match your request flow and show span-level latencies.
[06:30] Priya Nair: What about model drift and quality monitoring post-POC?
[06:34] Maya Lin: Redwood Optimize has a quality monitoring suite; for the POC we can enable basic regression alerts tied to eval sets and prompt sets. Post-POC we can demo the fuller feature set.
[06:45] Sam Parker: Any objections or blockers right now?
[06:48] Alex Rivera: Not blocker — main dependency is getting the sample data and network contacts. Also need final sign-off from security for any VPC peering.
[06:57] Priya Nair: We'll circle back on that.
[07:00] Sam Parker: Great. Last bit — I'll send proposed SOW, SAML/SSO onboarding doc, and SOC2 pack. Jordan will provision a tenant and generate API keys once we get Priya's admin email.
[07:12] Daniel Cho: I'll put Daniel.network@zenith into the thread for peering.
[07:15] Sam Parker: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with dates and the SOW.
[07:20] Alex Rivera: Thanks, talk soon.
closing_recap: Agreed 6-week POC with milestones: kickoff (week of 2026-01-20), access/setup by 2026-01-15, baseline hosted benchmarks week 1-2, dedicated tests week 3-4, mid-point review end week 5, exec readout week 6. Deliverables: SOW + pricing, security docs, test tenant + API keys, sample traffic and labeled eval set. Owners assigned for each action item.
